problems.form_value: exclusions says the 35 non-randomized participants 'are outside the analyzed sample', and n_analyzed is 791 (of 811 who took part)
problems.source_says: The PDF's own numbers rule out both claims at once. If 791 of the 811 participants were analyzed, only 20 were left out, so at least 15 of the 35 non-randomized participants must be inside the analyzed sample. Footnote 6 says all 35 worked alone, so they would sit in the individual arms (154 and 155). If instead all 35 are outside, at most 776 of the 811 were analyzed, and Table 1's 791 counts 15 people who are not among them. The document does not say which holds. The form should state this either-or and not assert both.
problems.quote: involving 811 participants from P&G’s Commercial and R&D functions. Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.
problems.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2 and fn. 6; p. 41, Table 1

problems.source_says: The PDF never prints 791. It is the screener's sum of the four Table 1 counts, a table the text calls 'an overview of the participants'. The only analyzed total the PDF states is 776, three times (abstract, introduction, Section 3.2). Table 1's units do equal the 550 regression observations, so 791 has table support, but the explicit text contradicts it and nothing in the PDF explains the 15-person surplus. The 791 reported for the Organization Science abstract comes from a version that is not on file. This check does not ask for a switch back to 776, because the PDF supports neither total cleanly. Keep 791 only as a disclosed Table 1 sum that conflicts with the text, or settle it from the journal version.
problems.quote: through a pre-registered field experiment with 776 professionals at Procter & Gamble, a global consumer packaged goods company.
problems.locator: p. 2, Abstract; p. 4, Introduction; p. 9, Section 3.2; p. 10 ('Table 1 provides an overview of the participants'); p. 41, Table 1

confirmed.statement: The arm counts match Table 1: 154 (Individual No AI), 155 (Individual + AI), 230 people in 115 teams (Team No AI), and 252 people in 126 teams (Team + AI).
The arm counts are people. Table 1 labels the team rows 'Team participants', 115 x 2 = 230 and 126 x 2 = 252, and the R&D share is 0.500 in both team arms, one R&D member per pair.

Table 1's units make up the 550 observations in Tables 2-4 and 10 (154 + 155 + 115 + 126 = 550), and Table 5 splits them 218 + 332. The Table 2 control-mean SE of 0.081 equals 1/sqrt(n) only for n = 151 to 154, which fits 154 control solutions.
The 550 are solutions, rated in 1,595 evaluations by 22 evaluators. The form puts them in the outcomes' n_units with unit 'output', not in the people counts.
confirmed.locator: p. 48, App. B.1; p. 49, App. B.4

confirmed.statement: The text states 811 workshop participants, 35 not randomly assigned (late entrants worked alone without AI, staff above band 3 worked alone with AI), and 776 analyzed. 811 - 35 = 776. The paper says results are consistent when the 35 are included.
confirmed.locator: p. 2, Abstract; p. 4; p. 9, Section 3.2 and fn. 6

confirmed.statement: Footnote 8 says a team with a member who failed to participate was nullified and the other member moved to an individual assignment, with no number given. The paper gives no count at assignment, so n_randomized = null (study and arms) and the 'not intention-to-treat' note follow the form-spec.
The paper has no flow diagram. Figure 1 is a 2x2 design graphic with no counts.

The emotion tables use 533 and 530 observations, split 262 + 271 and 259 + 271 by AI status. These fit within the 269 non-AI and 281 AI solutions, so they are not people counts. The form reports them only as observations.
Figure 12's y-axis reads 'Number of Participants', but by eye the Team + AI bars sum to roughly the 126 teams, not the 252 members. The form takes no count from Figure 12.
The paper has one study. The control groups repeated the task with AI after training, but the paper reports only the initial between-subject comparisons, so no one enters a coded contrast twice.

No other paper in the screening uses these participants. The PDF names none, only c052 files mention Procter & Gamble, and c051 (Dell'Acqua et al., Jagged Frontier) studies consultants. A blank sample_overlap is right.
confirmed.locator: pp. 1-54; candidates.json, c051; search of the forms folder

confirmed.statement: The participants quote is verbatim (35 words). The who, population, and country fields match: P&G Commercial and R&D professionals in four business units, enrolled through an upskilling initiative, randomized within Europe and Americas clusters, with no country named.
Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone under either total, 776 (text) or 791 (Table 1). The two individual arms alone hold 309 people.

summary: The per-arm people counts (154, 155, 230, 252) match Table 1 and the 550 analyzed solutions, and criterion 2 holds on S1 alone under either the text's 776 or Table 1's 791. But the study total of 791 is a Table 1 sum that the PDF never states and its text contradicts (811 took part, 35 not randomized, 776 analyzed), and the exclusions field says both that 791 people were analyzed and that all 35 non-randomized participants are outside the analyzed sample, which cannot both hold because 811 - 791 = 20.
